subject: Staging pool quota & short-term reservation for ZenApps pilot
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staging pool quota & short-term reservation for ZenApps pilot

Team —

ZenApps (Ravi copied below) wants to run a 6-week pilot starting the week of Nov 30. Product would like a dedicated staging pool that mirrors the Dedicated environment (same GPU class) to validate batching behavior and KV cache sizing before we flip to canary in prod. Key asks: 1) short-term reservation for 10x A100-equivalent GPUs for the first 3 weeks, declining to 4x thereafter; 2) an autoscaling policy exception so the pool can't scale below 4 nodes during peak test windows; 3) a quick cost estimate and confirmation of whether we can keep the pool in the us-west region.

I've attached the staging_quota_proposal (capacity profile + expected traffic shape) and a one-pager on the MVP scope.

Questions for infra/procurement: what lead time do you need to allocate the GPUs (CloudVendor vs Dedicated), and is there any policy reason we can't do the temporary reservation with an autoscale floor? If needed I can push a one-time approval from Sales Ops/Finance.

Next steps: can Dev/Karthik propose a minimal config and rough cost by EOD Monday? I'll loop in Ravi for timeline confirmation.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: 20261119-zenapps-staging_quota_proposal.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staging pool quota & short-term reservation for ZenApps pilot

On Thu, Nov 19, 2026 at 09:12, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
>
> ZenApps (Ravi copied below) wants to run a 6-week pilot starting the week of Nov 30...

Thanks for the summary. Quick answers from infra:
- We can provision a temporary pool in us-west for a short-term reservation; CloudVendor has availability for that window but it requires a 72-hour lead time for provisioning GPUs at scale.
- Autoscale floor: current org policy allows autoscale-floor exceptions for pilot/dedicated pools with an approvals trace (engineering lead + finance). We already have a PR template for exception requests (link in my signature).
- Minimal config suggestion (initial): 10 x A100-equivalent, node-level batching enabled, KV cache warmed from a snapshot during the first hour. After week 3, scale down to 4 nodes by policy-based schedule.

Estimated incremental cost (very rough): $28k/week at 10 nodes (inclusive of CloudVendor surcharges) -> ~84k for first 3 weeks, then ~11k/week for the reduced set. Karthik can refine with pricing models.

Action items:
1) Karthik: please produce an itemized pricing + margin impact by Monday EOD.
2) Hannah: if you approve the exception flow I'll submit the org-level autoscale-floor exception and tag Finance.
3) Marissa: can Sales Ops confirm if ZenApps is ok with a short-term pass-through for infra charges or do we absorb the pilot cost?

- Dev

[Attachment: infra-exception-template.md (text/plain) — referenced]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staging pool quota & short-term reservation for ZenApps pilot

Hannah/Dev —

Attached is a quick pricing sketch based on the traffic profile in the spreadsheet. Highlights:
- 10-node A100-equivalent pool (continuous 12-hour daily peak) -> ~$26.5k/week (we can take a small margin hit if Sales wants to subsidize).
- If we request a formal short-term reservation from CloudVendor (3-week block) they offer a 7% discount vs on-demand, but the contract needs a signed addendum.
- Autoscale-floor exception will increase risk of idle spend; I recommend a scheduled policy: floor at 4 nodes only during the defined test windows (UTC 15:00-23:00) to limit waste.

I'll push an itemized sheet to the Drive link Hannah shared and update SUP-2147 with the procurement ask.

Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer

[Attachment: 20261120-zenapps-pricing_sketch.csv (text/csv)]

From: Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@zenapps.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staging pool quota & short-term reservation for ZenApps pilot

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from ZenApps:
- Pilot start: Nov 30 is ideal; we need ~2 full business days of handoff with Redwood SREs to warm caches and run smoke tests.
- Budget: we have approval up to $60k for infra during the pilot; if Redwood can cover incremental overspend for the first week we can commit to a paid POC.
- We are fine with a scheduled autoscale-floor (15:00-23:00 UTC) if it reduces unexpected cost.

Please confirm provisioning lead time and whether Redwood will execute the CloudVendor addendum or if we need to sign on ZenApps' side.

—Ravi
Head of Platform
ZenApps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staging pool quota & short-term reservation for ZenApps pilot

Hannah — quick update from Sales Ops/Finance: we can approve the autoscale-floor exception and short-term reservation provided:
1) We have the procurement addendum signed by EOD Nov 24.
2) ZenApps signs a simple cost pass-through for week 1 if spend exceeds $60k, otherwise Redwood will absorb overruns up to $10k.
3) Engineering uploads the exception request in the PR template and tags Finance (DEV/OPS approval).

I'll coordinate the contract addendum with CloudVendor legal and loop Ravi if we need a counterparty signature. Karthik/Dev — please push the updated pricing sheet and the PR template link into the Drive folder; Hannah, please confirm you want me to execute the addendum on Redwood's side.

Marissa
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
